facts.claim: Brain freeze is a short frontal or temporal headache triggered when cold food, drink or air passes over the palate or the back of the throat.
By the diagnostic criteria, brain freeze resolves within 10 minutes after the cold stimulus is removed.
In a 2017 experiment, gulping 200 ml of ice water triggered brain freeze in 39 of 77 volunteers (51%), while pressing an ice cube to the palate triggered it in only 9 (12%).
With ice water, the pain started a median 15 seconds after drinking and was mostly described as stabbing.
In a 2002 randomised trial with 145 students, eating ice cream in under 5 seconds caused brain freeze in 27%, versus 13% when eating slowly over more than 30 seconds.
In a small 2012 study of 13 volunteers, the anterior cerebral artery dilated quickly as the pain began and narrowed again as the pain faded.
Brain freeze is common in the general population, especially among people with migraine.
The cold hits the palate, but the pain is felt in the forehead or temples: it is referred pain, not the brain itself freezing.
